rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: the back rank is the first rank on each side, where the king usually stays after castling. Here the black king is on g8, and the pawns on f7, g7 and h7 block the squares in front of it.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.p: Find the rook move that gives mate.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook checks on d8, along the eighth rank, and the king has no square, because its own pawns block the way out.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.revela: The rook goes to d8 and gives mate: the check comes along the eighth rank, and the pawns on f7, g7 and h7 take away the king's escape squares.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.err.h2h3.1: Advancing the pawn opens an escape square for your king, a good idea in positions like this, but it does not attack the black king.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.err.h2h3.2: With this move Black has a resource: the pawn goes to h6, and the king gains the h7 square to escape a check on the eighth rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.err.h2h3.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check on the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.err.g2g3.1: Advancing the pawn opens an escape square for your king, a good idea in positions like this, but it does not attack the black king.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.err.g2g3.2: With this move Black has a resource: the pawn goes to h6, and the king gains the h7 square to escape a check on the eighth rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.err.g2g3.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check on the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not check the black king. Look for the square on the eighth rank that the rook on d1 can reach.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the rook check.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.l1: This is the back-rank mate: the king is trapped on the back rank, and no black piece can capture the rook or block. The rook on b2 is off the eighth rank and cannot help.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex1.l2: In positions like this, an advanced pawn, such as on h6 for Black or on h3 for you, opens an escape square for the king. Giving your king an escape in time prevents this mate.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: the black king is on h8, trapped by the pawns on g7 and h7, and the bishop on d5 watches g8. The bishop on c8 stands between the rook on a8 and the one on f8.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.p: Find the rook move that gives mate on the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.certo: Yes, it is mate: the rook on f1 captures the one on f8 with check, and no black piece can recapture.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.revela: The rook on f1 captures the one on f8 with check and gives mate: the king has no square, and nobody recaptures.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.err.f1f7.1: The rook attacks the queen, but without check and on a square attacked by the rook on f8.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.err.f1f7.2: With this move Black has a resource: the rook on f8 captures yours, and the back rank is no longer the target.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.err.f1f7.3: Back to the position: look for the rook check on the eighth rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.fora: That move does not give mate. Look for the check on the eighth rank, where the black king has no square.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the check on the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.ideia.ex2.l1: The rook on a8 does not defend f8, because the bishop on c8 blocks the rank. In positions like this, the back-rank mate works when no piece defends the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.demos.mestres.1: Attack: now let us think from Black's side. This position is from a Lichess game between two titled players, Blueagle and MichaMichalek. The white king is on g1, behind the pawns on f2, g2 and h2.
rot.backRankMate.demos.mestres.2: The rook on c8 goes down the open file and checks on the first rank. No white piece defends that rank: it is a back-rank mate.
rot.backRankMate.demos.semDefensor.1: Attack: back to White, in a Lichess game between two titled players, Zeveraar-Glen and sh20032006. The black king is on f8, with the knight on e7 and the pawns on f7 and g7 in front of it.
rot.backRankMate.demos.semDefensor.2: The rook on d1 goes to d8 and checks along the eighth rank. It watches e8 and g8 itself, and no black piece can capture the rook or block: it is mate.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.1: Attack: the black rook on d1 threatens to capture yours on e1 with mate, but it is your move, and the black king on g8 is also trapped by its pawns.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.p: Find the queen check that the black king cannot escape with a king move.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.certo: Yes: the queen checks on a8, along the eighth rank, and the threat on e1 has to wait.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.revela: The queen goes to a8 and checks along the eighth rank, and the threat on e1 has to wait.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.err.f3f7: The queen captures the pawn on f7 with check, but none of your pieces defends that square.
With this move Black has a resource: the king captures the queen, and the rook on d1 still attacks yours on e1.
Back to the position: look for the check on Black's back rank.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.2: The king has no square: f8 and h8 are on the line of the check, and the pawns block the rest. Black has to block.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.3: The rook comes back from d1 and blocks on d8, Black's only move. There it is attacked by the queen and has no defender.
rot.backRankMate.demos.interpor.4: The queen captures the rook with mate. In positions like this, the piece that blocks only stops the check if something defends it.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.1: Attack: Black again. The queen on c3 has two checks on the first rank, on e1 and on c1, and the white rook on b1 defends that rank.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.p: Before the check, count who attacks and who defends each square. Which queen check works?
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.certo: Yes, the check on c1. See why it works and the one on e1 does not.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.revela: The right check is on c1: there the rook on c7 attacks too, from behind the queen.
The queen checks on e1, and it looks like a back-rank mate. But on e1 only the queen attacks.
With this move White has a resource: the rook on b1 captures the queen, and Black is left without it.
Back to the position: look for the square on the first rank that two black pieces attack.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.2: On c1 the rook on c7 attacks too, from behind the queen. That is two pieces against one defender.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.6: The rook on b1 captures the queen, the only move. Now the rank has no defender.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.7: The rook on c7 recaptures with mate. On e1 only the queen attacked, and the rook on b1 would capture it with no recapture.
rot.backRankMate.demos.excecao.8: In positions like this, with one defender on the rank, the back-rank mate needs two pieces against the same square.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.1: Attack: Black again. The rook on c8 wants to go down to c1, on the first rank, but the white king on b1 defends that square.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.2: The rook goes down to c1 with check, but no black piece defends that square.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.3: The king captures the rook. Here the king itself was the defender of the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.4: Back to the position: before the mate, a check can drive the king away from the square it defends.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.5: The knight goes to d2, gives check and also attacks the rook on b3. The rook on c8 watches c1 and c2.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.6: The king goes to a1, the only move. From there it no longer defends c1.
rot.backRankMate.demos.xequeAntes.7: The rook goes down to c1 with mate: it watches b1, and the bishop on f1 blocks the rook on h1. The check first took the defender out of the way.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.valeAqui.enunci: Back to White. The queen on d7 reaches the eighth rank. Does the back-rank mate work here? Play as White and find the best move.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.valeAqui.fim: On e8 only the queen attacked, and the rook on c8 captured it. On d8 the rook on d1 attacked too: the black rook captured the queen, and your rook recaptured with mate.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.valeAqui.err.d7: With the check on e8 you give up the queen: the rook on c8 defends that square, and only the queen attacked it.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.valeAqui.err.d1: The rook attacks the queen on c5, but without check: Black captures the a3 pawn with the queen, and the game is equal. Look for a check on the eighth rank.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.valeAqui.err.e4: The pawn advances without check and opens your bishop's diagonal, but Black, a knight up, has time to defend. Look for the check they cannot stop.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.valeAqui.err.e2: That move is not a check, and Black, a knight up, gains time to defend the back rank. Look for the check they cannot stop.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.cobrir.enunciad: Now let us think from Black's side. The white rook on e8 attacks your rook on b8, and the white king is on g1, behind its pawns. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.cobrir.fim: The rook checked on b1, and White's only defence was to bring the rook from e8 to e1. With no defender there, your rook captured it with mate.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.cobrir.err.b8e8: Capturing the rook on e8 wins back material, but White is still a queen and a bishop up. Look for the check on the back rank.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.semRoque.enunci: Back to White. The black king has not castled and stands on f8, with the pawn on e7 and the bishop on g7 beside it. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.semRoque.fim: The rook checked on d8 and controlled the eighth rank: the pawn on e7 and the bishop on g7 boxed the king in, and no black piece could capture the rook or block. The back-rank mate works without castling too.
rot.backRankMate.pratica.semRoque.err.e3: The queen trade leaves the game equal. Look for the check on the eighth rank: the black king has no escape square.
